rationale: Treat this as a wiring question. The receptor FGFR1, driven by Api5-induced FGF2, sits above both kinase arms; when the receptor itself was blocked, both arms lost signal. Each selective compound hits only its own arm, and neither one moved Api5 or FGF2, so whatever reaches the other arm from the receptor is unaltered. Are the arms wired in series or side by side? Their outputs say side by side. Stopping Akt fixed acinar size, cell number, roundness and the Ki-67 index, while filled lumens and mislocalised Laminin V, GM130 and E-cadherin persisted. Stopping MEK/ERK fixed size and proliferation and also emptied the lumens and put the three junction and polarity proteins back where they belong. An arm that fed the other would have taken the other's phenotypes down with it; neither did. Side-by-side arms with an intact shared input predict flat cross readouts, so pERK1/2 under the Akt compound is unchanged and pAkt T308 under UO126 is unchanged. The familiar feedback story, where stopping MEK lifts a brake and pushes Akt phosphorylation up, needs the stopped arm to signal back to the receptor; nothing here changes ligand or receptor, so no rise is expected either. The remaining two readouts simply report that each drug reached its target, which the reverted phenotypes already imply: pAkt T308 falls with the Akt inhibitor, and pERK1/2 falls with UO126.
